t:
(a) 
Effective October 1, 1980, the Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate is authorized to appoint and fix the compensation of four garage attendants at not to exceed $14,100 per annum each.
 
    (b) 
If, and to the extent that, positions established by subsection (a) are first filled by individuals transferred under subsection (a)(1) of the first section, the Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate is authorized to fix, in lieu of the compensation prescribed in subsection (a), the compensation—

        (1) 
of not more than two of such positions so filled at not to exceed $16,560 per annum each;
 
        (2) 
of one of such positions so filled at not to exceed $15,485 per annum; and
 
        (3) 
of one of such positions so filled at not to exceed $14,390 per annum.

Compensation fixed under this subsection for a position first filled by an individual transferred under subsection (a)(1) of the first section shall cease to be applicable with respect to such position on the date that such individual first ceases to occupy such position.
  
    (c) During any period with respect to which subsection (b) is applicable to a position occupied by an individual described in such subsection, such individual shall be credited, for purposes of longevity compensation, as authorized by section 106 (a), (b), and (d) of the Legislative Branch Appropriation Act, 1963 (2 U.S.C. 60j), for service performed by such individual in the position of garage attendant, as an employee of the Architect of the Capitol, as certified to the Secretary of the Senate by the Architect of the Capitol.

fable.w: This section only authorizes the Senate Sergeant at Arms to appoint garage attendants and set their pay, and credits prior service certified by the Architect of the Capitol. The tempting reading is that the certification to the Secretary of the Senate is a form of coordination, but every actor is a legislative-branch official or employee inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision.
fable.s: the Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper of the Senate is authorized to appoint and fix the compensation of four garage attendants at not to exceed $14,100 per annum each

opus.w: This section lets the Senate Sergeant at Arms hire garage attendants, set their pay, and credit their prior service toward longevity pay. The only interaction it describes is the Architect of the Capitol certifying service to the Secretary of the Senate, and both are federal officials. Coordination inside the government is not participation, and no outside party is consulted or given a role.
opus.s: as an employee of the Architect of the Capitol, as certified to the Secretary of the Senate by the Architect of the Capitol
opus.b: The tempting reading is that the Architect of the Capitol's certification to the Secretary of the Senate counts as a formal step before a decision. It doesn't, because both are part of the federal government (the legislative branch). Everything else in the section is about hiring staff and setting their pay.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the appointment and compensation of federal employees (garage attendants) and details the crediting of their service time. The interaction described involves the Architect of the Capitol certifying service to the Secretary of the Senate. Both the Architect of the Capitol and the Senate are entities within the federal government. Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination and administrative procedure, not participation by parties outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: such individual shall be credited, for purposes of longevity compensation, as authorized by section 106 (a), (b), and (d) of the Legislative Branch Appropriation Act, 1963 (2 U.S.C. 60j), for service performed by such individual in the position of garage attendant, as an employee of the Architect of the Capitol, as certified to the Secretary of the Senate by the Architect of the Capitol.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Architect of the Capitol" certifying service to the "Secretary of the Senate" constitutes coordination between government entities. However, both the Architect of the Capitol and the Senate are part of the federal government (specifically, the legislative branch and its support agencies). Therefore, this is intra-governmental coordination, not participation by an outside party. Furthermore, the section primarily deals with hiring and compensation for federal employees (garage attendants), which does not involve public consultation or advisory boards with non-federal members.
